idiom_name: symbol table of { nud, led, lbp } functions (Crockford TDOP shape)
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the parselet hierarchy becomes a plain object or Map from token type to { nud, led, lbp }, and the loop is a while that compares the next token's binding power - Crockford's TDOP chapter builds exactly this, with token objects inheriting nud/led from symbol prototypes. Functions close over the parser, so no context object is needed and operator tables extend at runtime, which is why Pratt parsers are the common choice for embedded expression evaluators and language toys; there is no standard-library parsing facility, and grammars beyond expressions usually go to a generator (Peggy, Chevrotain, nearley). Keep the handlers as free functions or call them as object properties, and distinguish an unknown token from a token whose binding power is legitimately zero.
pitfalls: Symbol handlers are methods on shared objects: extracting symbols.get(type).led and calling it detached loses this in the prototype style Crockford used; call handlers as properties or keep them as free functions.
An unknown token reads as binding power 0, so a missing rule silently ends the expression instead of raising an error; test rule existence separately from the value of lbp.
Long chains and deep nesting recurse once per operator and engines do not optimise tail calls, so a depth counter keeps the failure a parse error rather than a RangeError.
